input.quote: 12.4 For eighteen months after termination Customer will not solicit or engage any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term.
input.rationale: § 12.4 imposes a one-way restriction on us only, runs 18 months post-termination, covers any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term (not just personnel involved in the services), extends to "engage" (an effective no-hire), and contains no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out. It therefore fails the fallback on every material term (mutuality, scope, trigger, carve-outs, no no-hire) and the no-hire element edges into walk-away territory. It also conflicts with § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we have made no no-hire commitment. Redline deletes § 12.4 to reach the preferred position, with the narrow mutual fallback offered in the comment.

proposal.summary: Delete the one-way 18-month non-solicit/no-engage binding Customer (§ 12.4), consistent with § 12.3.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We do not accept non-solicitation or no-hire restrictions on us, so we have deleted § 12.4; it also contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have given no no-hire commitment. If Vendor needs protection, we can accept a mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, for 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertising and unsolicited approaches and no restriction on hiring.
